clue.text: He wrote fliers in dynastic style?

parts.note: erns or ernes are sea eagles, so fliers in crossword terms
the Ming were a Chinese dynasty, so doing things in their style is in the Ming way

explanation.surface: A question about an author who wrote about birds in a grand imperial manner.
explanation.definitionFit: The American novelist wrote The Old Man and the Sea and A Farewell to Arms, so is an author.

clue.text: Broadcasts went for a high rate?

parts.note: to air something is to broadcast it
peed is a slang word for went, as in went to the toilet

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether broadcasts were aired at a fast pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' is the colloquial euphemism for relieving oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: The speed of an aircraft relative to the air around it is a rate of travel up high.

clue.text: Potential bloomer, perhaps, the ultimate in licentiousness — function of crossword setters that's disgusting

indicators.note: the ultimate in a word is its final letter

parts.note: a do is a party or function, and one held by the setters is ours
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A rambling tale of a blunder at a crossword setters' party that turned seedy and revolting.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is both a blunder and a British loaf with a rounded, slashed top; the definition uses the bread sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A starter-leavened bread could be shaped and baked as a bloomer loaf, so it is a potential example.

clue.text: Note provin' an irritation for soul singer

parts.note: F is a musical note
something that rankles is an irritation, and the dropped g in provin' is copied in ranklin'

explanation.surface: A musical note becomes annoying for a soul vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'provin'' tells you the synonym also drops its final g.
explanation.definitionFit: Aretha Franklin, the Queen of Soul, was one of the great soul vocalists.

clue.text: General gossip curtailed in African city

parts.note: an aga is an Ottoman military commander

indicators.note: curtailed means the tail, or last letter, is cut off

parts.note: dirt is scandalous gossip

explanation.surface: A general's gossip is cut short while in an African city.
explanation.definitionFit: Agadir is a port city on the Atlantic coast of Morocco.

clue.text: Small crustacean also caught by one with a basket?

indicators.note: caught by means held within, so the word for also sits inside

parts.note: a shopper carries a basket
and means also

explanation.surface: A tiny sea creature is also caught by someone carrying a basket.
explanation.definitionFit: This little amphipod jumps about on beaches, a small crustacean.

clue.text: See 6
Words of defiance noted as some deliveries from a West Indian fast bowler arrive

parts.note: Wes Hall was a celebrated West Indian fast bowler of the 1960s
in cricket an over is six deliveries
to come is to arrive

explanation.surface: A cricket picture of balls from a Caribbean paceman arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: The civil rights protest song is a set of defiant words set to music, hence noted.

clue.text: Animal in love with rough skin?

indicators.note: the skin of a word is its outside, so the first and last letters of rough are taken

parts.note: taken as written
love is nil in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A beast with a thick hide is described as loving rough skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough skin' looks like a description of the animal's hide, but 'skin' means take the outer letters of 'rough'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinoceros, shortened in everyday speech, is a large thick-skinned mammal.

clue.text: Duty beyond doctor with a degree? Nonsense!

indicators.note: beyond places the word for duty after the other pieces

parts.note: to doctor something is to tamper with or fix it, as in to rig it
an MA is a Master of Arts degree
a duty is a part or function you perform, a role

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a job that ranks above a doctor with an extra qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, confused and pointless procedure or story is dismissed as rubbish; the exclamation fits an exclamatory use.

clue.text: Dinner she cooked is cherished

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters have been worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A meal a woman prepared is treasured.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held sacred and preserved with reverence is treasured, a close synonym.

clue.text: Principal characters of Degas' erotic painting that have intensity

indicators.note: principal characters are the leading letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Degas's racy pictures are said to have a certain strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principal characters' looks like the people in the painting, but it means the first letters of the five words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Depth of colour or feeling is its richness or strength, a standard sense.

clue.text: Grossly below the belt, West Indian male seeking English dismissal (hard to get out) coming to grips with length finally, finding famous slip in cricket?

definitions.text: Grossly below the belt, West Indian male seeking English dismissal (hard to get out) coming to grips with length finally, finding famous slip in cricket?

parts.words: Grossly below the belt, West Indian male seeking English dismissal (hard to get out) coming to grips with length finally, finding famous slip in cricket?
parts.note: the clue describes a radio commentator's famous verbal blunder: West Indian bowler Michael Holding running in at England batsman Peter ..., and the phrase heard as a rude double entendre

explanation.surface: A long tale of a West Indian fast bowler trying to get out a stubborn English batsman, ending in a well-known slip.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'slip' is not the fielding position but a slip of the tongue, attributed to the BBC cricket commentator Brian Johnston; 'below the belt' flags its innuendo.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the celebrated commentary gaffe in which the names of two players formed an unintended rude meaning.

clue.text: Right to leave out opener for test

indicators.note: leaving out the opener drops the first letter of the word found for right

parts.note: moral means right in the ethical sense

explanation.surface: In cricket, a captain may be right to drop an opening batsman for a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as cricket selection: 'opener' is an opening batsman and 'test' a Test match, but here 'opener' is just a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken examination, as opposed to a written paper, is a kind of test.

clue.text: Drunk agreed on quaffing a drink

indicators.note: quaffing means swallowing, so the anagram takes in the a
drunk means the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A tipsy person agrees to down a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' shuffles AGREED ON into ORANGEDE, and 'quaffing' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy citrus soft drink is a kind of beverage.

clue.text: In conclusion, a god refused repellent Turkish leader

indicators.note: repellent, read as driving back, signals that the hidden letters are read backwards
in signals that the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A story ends with a deity turned away as repulsive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' hides NAGODRE across 'conclusion, a god refused'; 'repellent' then turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Recep Tayyip Erdogan has been the president, and before that prime minister, of Turkey.

clue.text: Officer lassoing horse and a buffalo

indicators.note: lassoing means roping in, so the officer's letters go round the others

parts.note: CO is short for commanding officer
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A cowboy officer ropes a horse and a buffalo.
explanation.definitionFit: The carabao is the water buffalo of the Philippines, a specific kind.

clue.text: Scale, perhaps, that would be put in front of an organ?

definitions.text: Scale, perhaps, that would be put in front of an organ?

parts.words: Scale, perhaps, that would be put in front of an organ?
parts.note: a scale from a fish of the cod family is a fish fragment; read the other way the word is a pouch worn over the male genitals

explanation.surface: A musical scale placed before playing a church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scale' and 'organ' suggest music; the scale is a fish's, and the organ is anatomical.
explanation.definitionFit: This flap or pouch was worn in front of the groin on men's breeches in the 15th and 16th centuries.

clue.text: See 13
Isle, a state

parts.note: IOW is the abbreviation for the Isle of Wight, an island off England's south coast

explanation.surface: An island is described as a state, as if listing territories.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is one of the fifty United States, in the Midwest.

clue.text: See 13
See 13
Stretch too far right in Spanish city, deporting first of immigrants

indicators.note: in places right inside what remains of the city
deporting means sending out, so a letter leaves the city

parts.note: Oviedo is a city in Asturias in northern Spain

indicators.note: first of means just the opening letter of immigrants

explanation.surface: A Spanish city deports incoming migrants and goes too far.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something to excess, exaggerating or overcooking it, is to push it beyond reasonable limits.

clue.text: Swallow travelling westward over a prison camp

indicators.note: over is used here in the sense of covering, so the turned word goes round the a
in an across answer travelling westward means reading right to left

parts.note: to glug is to swallow in big gulps

explanation.surface: A bird flying west passes over a prison camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' reads as the bird, but is the verb. 'Travelling westward' turns GLUG into GULG, and the A sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet system of forced-labour camps gave its name to any harsh political prison camp.

clue.text: Some hard stuff in bottle

definitions.meaning: small hard particles of stone or sand
bottle is British slang for courage or nerve

explanation.surface: Some strong liquor kept in a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard stuff' suggests spirits, which suits a bottle, but it is gravelly matter, and 'bottle' means pluck.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: tiny stony particles, and determination or courage of character.

clue.text: Remedy initially cutting disease on the surface in humans, for example?

definitions.text: on the surface in humans, for example?

indicators.note: cutting means the letter slices into the word for disease

parts.note: an epidemic is a widespread outbreak of disease

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of remedy is used

explanation.surface: A cure starts to bite into an illness that shows on human skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the outer layer of skin, which in people and other animals lies at the body's surface.

clue.text: Irregular account describing spirit before cricket game

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing round, so the account letters enclose the rest
before puts the spirit ahead of the cricket game

parts.note: a peri is a fairy-like spirit of Persian legend
an ODI is a one-day international cricket match

explanation.surface: A report tells of drinking spirits before a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests a drink, but it is a peri, a Persian fairy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without a regular period or cycle is irregular, a technical synonym.

clue.text: This writer's after office material

indicators.note: after puts the writer's words behind the office

parts.note: a den is a private study or office room
this writer is the setter, so this writer's is I am, shortened to I'm

explanation.surface: A writer claims to come after the office stationery.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing cotton twill fabric, so a type of material.
